report.source_text: The patient, therefore, underwent umbilectomy, excision of umbilical endometriosis, lysis of adhesions and umbilical hernia repair under general anaesthesia. A circumferential incision was made around the umbilicus using a scalpel. This was taken down to the subcutaneous tissue using electrocautery. The endometrioma was densely adherent to the umbilical skin as expected, as well as the hernia sac, the omental fat contents of the umbilical hernia sac and the anterior rectus sheath (see figure 3). This lesion was hence excised en masse with a wide margin, resulting in a large defect in the anterior abdominal wall (see figure 4). The defect was closed primarily using synthetic mesh and the skin edges were approximated using staples, leaving a subcutaneous drain (see figure 5). The specimen was sent to pathology for analysis.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Surgical pathology revealed cystic endometriosis within subcutaneous tissue, consistent with umbilical endometrioma.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A nulliparous woman in her 40s with hypertension, obesity (BMI 37), uterine fibroids, abnormal uterine bleeding, and dyschezia presented with cyclic umbilical pain and bleeding coinciding with menses. She had a significant surgical history of two abdominal myomectomies via Pfannenstiel incision with documented endometrial breach in both procedures. Physical examination revealed a 3 cm blood-filled cyst at the umbilicus consistent with umbilical endometriosis. MRI imaging confirmed an umbilical endometrioma. Medical management with medroxyprogesterone acetate was attempted without relief, and the patient was not a candidate for combined oral contraceptives due to hypertension and elevated BMI. She underwent umbilectomy with excision of the umbilical endometriosis, lysis of adhesions, and umbilical hernia repair under general anesthesia. The endometrioma was densely adherent to the umbilical skin, hernia sac, omental fat, and anterior rectus sheath, and was excised en masse with wide margins. The defect was closed primarily with synthetic mesh. Surgical pathology of the specimen confirmed cystic endometriosis within the subcutaneous tissue, consistent with umbilical endometrioma.
